To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in hepatocyte culture, HBV genotype has a limited role in viral sensitivity to interferon, and the efficacy of interferon is determined more by cellular interferon response.
in the cell–culture‐based HBV infection model, sensitivity of HBV replication to IFN‐alpha in hepatocytes was determined more by the cellular interferon response rather than the viral genotype.
the sensitivity of HB virus to interferon‐alpha (IFN‐alpha) in hepatocytes is not determined by the genotype of the virus, but by the cell‐specific interferon (IFN) response of the host cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the efficacy of IFNs against HBV varies across genotypes and hepatocyte models.
how hepatitis B virus ( HBV ) is affected by interferon‐α ( IFN‐α ) in hepatocytes and the role of viral genotype in this process.
the antiviral efficacy of interferon‐alpha (IFN‐alpha) against hepatitis B virus (HCV) in hepatocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the efficacy of IF‐α in HBV‐infection cell culture models is more associated with cell‐intrinsic response to IF‐α than with HBV genotype.
IFN‐α efficacy is not associated with HBV genotype but with cellular interferon‐response capacity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the efficacy of IFNs against HBV in the hepatocyte‐based cell culture models is mainly determined by the IFN response rather than by the viral genotype.
the sensitivity of HBVs to interferon‐alpha (IFN‐alpha) in hepatocytes is primarily determined by cellular interferon response, not by viral genotypes.
IFN‐α sensitivity of HBV in hepatocyte is more associated with the cellular IFN response rather than the viral genotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antiviral activity of IFN against HBV in cell‐based infection models is more determined by the cell‐specific interferon response rather than by the viral genotype.
the sensitivity of HBVs to IFN‐alpha in infected hepatocytes is more related to the cell‐inherent IFN response than to viral genotypes.
the efficacy of interferon‐α against HBsAg and HBV DNA in primary human hepatocytes is much higher than that in HepaRG cells or HepG2 cells.
